body:
A pod vape is a small battery unit that uses a snap-in pod holding the liquid and coil. It is popular because it is compact, easy to use and less fiddly than a tank, and it sits comfortably between a disposable and a box mod. But pod systems come in several varieties, with different pod types, battery sizes and activation methods, and choosing between them is easier when you know what each means. This guide explains what a pod vape is, how closed and open pods differ, what to look for, how to choose liquid, how to set up and care for a pod device, common problems and who a pod system suits. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## What a pod vape is
A pod vape has two main parts: a battery section, usually with a sensor or a button and a charging port, and a pod, which clicks into it. The pod contains the liquid reservoir, the wick and, in most designs, the coil. When the pod is empty or the coil wears out, you replace or refill the pod and keep the battery. The design keeps maintenance low, which is why pods suit many beginners. See [how does a vape work](/blog/how-does-a-vape-work/) and [parts of a vape](/blog/parts-of-a-vape-glossary/).

## Closed pods
Closed pods arrive pre-filled and are thrown away or recycled when empty. They are convenient and leak-resistant, but you are limited to the flavors the manufacturer sells for that device. Many [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) in our catalog are of this type. You buy a pack of pods in a flavor, click one in and use it. When it is finished, you replace it. They suit people who want simplicity above all.

## Open pods
Open pods are refillable. You fill them with your own e-liquid and replace the coil when it wears out. They cost less over time and give unlimited flavor choice, at the price of a little extra effort. You need to learn to fill without overfilling, to prime a new coil and to choose liquid that suits the pod. See [how to fill a pod without leaks](/blog/how-to-fill-a-pod-without-leaks/).

### Closed or open: how to decide
If you want zero fuss, choose closed pods. If you want flavor choice and lower running costs, choose open pods. If you are not sure, start with closed pods, and move to open when you are comfortable. Many adults keep both.

## Things to look for
- **Pod capacity:** typically 2 mL, which is the limit in many regions.
- **Coil type:** mesh coils give smoother flavor. See [what is a mesh coil](/blog/what-is-a-mesh-coil/).
- **Battery:** 400 to 1,000 mAh is typical for pod devices. See [mAh, puffs and battery life](/blog/mah-puffs-and-battery-life-how-they-relate/).
- **Draw activation:** auto-draw is easy, button-fire gives more control. See [auto-draw vs button-fire](/blog/auto-draw-vs-button-fire-vapes/).
- **Charging port:** USB-C is common and convenient.
- **Seal and build:** a good seal keeps leaks away.
- **Availability of pods:** make sure replacements are easy to find.

## Choosing liquid
Pods pair well with nicotine salts. Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) designed for them, and check our [salts versus freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/) guide. A 50/50 PG/VG ratio suits most pods; see [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/). Avoid thick, high-VG liquid in small pods, because it wicks poorly and can burn the coil. Choose a strength you are comfortable with; see [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/).

## Setting up a pod device
1. Charge the battery fully.
2. If the pod is refillable, fill it below the line, without splashing the center.
3. Seat the pod firmly until it clicks.
4. Let it rest for five to ten minutes, so the coil soaks.
5. Take a few gentle puffs, then use as normal.

## Care tips
Do not overfill, keep pods upright when storing, and let a new coil soak before the first puff. Our guide on [priming a coil](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/) covers it. Wipe the contacts occasionally with a dry cotton bud. Replace the pod or coil when flavor fades. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/).

## Common problems
- **Leaking:** usually overfilling or a poor seat. See [leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/).
- **Weak vapor:** a worn coil, low liquid or a low battery.
- **Burnt taste:** a dry wick or worn coil. See [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/).
- **Gurgling:** excess liquid. See [fixing a gurgling vape](/blog/vape-gurgling-sound-fix/).

## A worked example
You choose an open pod kit with a 2 mL pod and a 600 mAh battery for about $22. You buy a 30 mL bottle of nicotine salt liquid, 50/50, for about $12. You fill the pod to the line, wait ten minutes and use it. A pod lasts about a week with regular use before the coil needs replacing, at about $4 for a two-pack of coils or pods. A bottle lasts about three weeks. Your monthly cost is roughly $17 to $20. If you had used disposables at about $18 for 20 days, your monthly cost would be about $27. The pod system saves a little each month, and you can choose your flavor.

## Who a pod system suits
People who want a compact device, a simple routine, lower running costs than disposables and a choice of flavors. If you want the most control, look at box mods. If you want zero upkeep, look at disposables. See [disposable vs pod vs box mod](/blog/disposable-vs-pod-vs-box-mod/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### How long does a pod last?
A pod or coil lasts from several days to a couple of weeks, depending on use and liquid.

### Can I use any liquid in a refillable pod?
Use liquid designed for pods, usually nicotine salts at about 50/50.

### Can I refill a closed pod?
Closed pods are not designed to be refilled. Do not try.

### Are pods interchangeable between brands?
No. Pods are specific to the device. Check the model.

### What if the pod does not fit?
Check that it is the right model, and that the contacts are clean. Do not force it.

## Shop
Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Choosing between pod systems
When two pod kits look alike, the details decide. Compare the battery size, the pod capacity, the charging port, the draw style and the availability and price of pods. A kit with a slightly bigger battery and easy-to-find pods can be a better buy than a cheaper one with obscure pods. Check that the pods are in stock, and that you can buy them in packs. If a pod type is discontinued, your device becomes useless, so choose a popular system.

## Costs of running a pod system
Running costs include pods or coils, liquid and charging. A pod or coil at about $4 for a pack of two lasts a couple of weeks. A 30 mL bottle at about $12 lasts several weeks. So a regular user spends about $15 to $20 a month. Compare that with the cost of disposables for your own use, and decide.

## Pods and nicotine strength
Pod systems are designed for nicotine salts, which are smooth at higher strengths. A typical strength is 20 to 50 mg/mL. Start with a strength you are comfortable with, and avoid assuming that a higher number is better. If you are unsure, read the strength guide, and ask us. See [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/).

## What a good routine looks like
Fill the pod when it is half empty, not when it is dry. Replace the coil or pod when flavor fades. Charge the device when it is low. Wipe the contacts weekly. Store the device upright, away from heat. A simple routine keeps a pod system working well, and it takes only a few minutes a week.

## When a pod system is not for you
If you dislike filling, priming and replacing parts, a disposable may suit you better. If you want maximum vapor and control, a box mod may. There is no shame in changing your mind. The best device is the one you enjoy using, and the one that fits your routine.

## Frequently asked questions about pods
### What does a pod cost?
Prices vary by brand and pack size. A pack of two pods or coils is typically a few dollars. Check each listing.

### Can I buy pods for any kit?
Only the pods designed for your device. Check the model name.

### Why do pods have 2 mL capacity?
Many regions limit pod size, and a small pod suits a small device.

### Can I mix flavors in one pod?
It is better to empty and rinse refillable pods between flavors, or to use a fresh pod. Mixing can leave odd tastes.

### How should I store spare pods?
Upright, in a cool, dry place, away from children and pets.

### What if the flavor tastes weak in a new pod?
Let it rest and soak. If it is still weak, the coil may be faulty. Contact us if it is from us.

## A closing checklist
Before you buy a pod system, check that you know whether the pods are closed or open, what a replacement pod costs, whether the battery and port suit you, which liquid to use, how to prime a coil and where to buy spares. If you can answer all six, you are ready. If not, ask us, and we will help you work out which system and which liquid suit your habits.
